steps.message:
Fixed. The generated aliases now put all exports inside the command substitution, matching what the tests expect:

- `thefuck/shells/bash.py` — now emits `alias fuck='TF_CMD=$(TF_ALIAS=fuck PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 TF_SHELL_ALIASES=$(alias) thefuck $(fc -ln -1)) && eval $TF_CMD'` (with `&& history -s $TF_CMD` when `alter_history` is set).
- `thefuck/shells/zsh.py` — same structure with `fc -ln -1 | tail -n 1` and `print -s $TF_CMD`.

Previously `TF_ALIAS` was exported before the `alias` builtin (bash) and `TF_CMD=$(thefuck ...)` ran `thefuck` without `TF_ALIAS`/`TF_SHELL_ALIASES` in its environment (zsh), so the correction command saw the wrong alias context.

Verification: `pytest` isn't installed in this environment (no pip/pytest modules), so I couldn't run the test suite directly. Instead I loaded both modules with stubbed dependencies and confirmed the output strings satisfy every assertion in `test_app_alias` and `test_app_alias_variables_correctly_set` in `tests/shells/test_bash.py` and `tests/shells/test_zsh.py`, including the `alter_history` suffixes.
